_schema: One JSON file per part category (parts.md). Two tiers now live side by side: `specs` is physics-bearing, and that rule is unchanged — if a spec does not feed the physics, it does not belong in `specs`. `catalog` is browsing metadata: a field is admitted there only if it is a factual, checkable property of the real product AND is needed to navigate the catalog at scale — colour, price and vendor links are still banned by name, from either block. 'arm_mm' is centre-to-motor and is the sleeper spec — it is squared in the parallel axis theorem, so a 7" frame has roughly 4x the roll inertia of a 3" from geometry alone. 'max_prop_inches' and 'motor_mount' drive compatibility warnings only; Lothal warns, it never blocks. 'stack_mount' is the centre-plate bolt pattern the FC/ESC stack sandwiches into — it is geometry-bearing (it is where the stack is drawn and what it is checked against), not physics-bearing: no mount position reaches the mass model.

parts.name: Nazgul Evoque F5 V2 (O4)
parts.source: iFlight 'Nazgul Evoque F5 V2 O4 Frame Kit' product page (shop.iflight.com, product 2283): weight 249±5 g, wheelbase 223 mm (DeadCat), 6 mm arms, 20x20/O3.0 mm stack, 16x16 mm motor mount. arm_mm is the published wheelbase halved, which is the motor radius; the frame is a DEADCAT, so the four motors are not on a square and this project's X layout is an approximation of its geometry — it is exact for mass, which is what data/validation/builds.json reads it for, and approximate for inertia.

parts.name: Nazgul Evoque F5 V3
parts.source: iFlight 'Nazgul Evoque F5 V3 Frame Kit' product page (shop.iflight.com, product 2407): weight 256±10 g, wheelbase 236 mm (DeadCat default) / 239 mm (True X), 6 mm arms, 20x20/O3.0 mm stack, 16x16 mm motor mount. arm_mm is the DeadCat wheelbase halved; same approximation note as the V2 above.

parts.name: GEP-MK5 O4 Pro Wide X
parts.source: GEPRC 'GEP-MK5 O4 Pro Wide X Frame' product page (geprc.com/product/gep-mk5-o4-pro-wide-x-frame/), 'Wide X Specifications' block: 'Weight: 165.1g ± 10g', 'Wheelbase: 225mm', 'Arm Thickness: 5.0mm', 'FC Mounting Pattern: 30.5mm * 30.5mm', 'Motor Mounting Pattern: 16mm * 16mm / 19mm * 19mm', 'Recommended Prop：5-inch', '3K carbon fiber frame'. arm_mm is the published wheelbase halved, which is the motor radius. motor_mount is the SMALLER of the two published patterns, which is the one the SPEEDX2 2107.5's Φ26.83 mm base can carry — a 19x19 pattern has a 26.87 mm diagonal, wider than the motor's own base. WHAT THE 165.1 g INCLUDES IS NOT STATED, and that omission is the point: the page's 'Includes' list carries '1 x GEP-MK5 O4 Pro Frame' as one line and then '1 x 3D printouts pack', '1 x Screw pack', the Velcro and rubber straps and the anti-slip pads as SEPARATE lines, which reads as the weight being the frame proper. iFlight state their Evoque frame-kit weights the same way — one number, no inventory — and the two vendors' numbers are 84 g apart for the same size class.
